title: Level 4 (Expert) - A-18
notes:
West leads the ♦K against 4♠. South's possible losers are 1 club and 3 hearts. South should play to set up the club suit without allowing East on lead to play through South's ♥K.

The correct line of play ensures the contract whenever clubs are 3-2 and spades are not 4-0. Declarer should allow West to hold the opening lead with the ♦K. The basic plan will be to discard declarer's third club on the ♦A and then ruff out the club suit, eventually reaching dummy in trumps to enjoy the long clubs.

When West doesn't switch to a trump at trick 2, declarer can further improve his chances and make the contract when West has only 1 club. Declarer should discard a club loser on the ♦A and cash a top club.

Next, South should travel back to his hand with a trump and lead a club towards the dummy. If West has a singleton club, it does him no good to ruff. South wins in dummy and ruffs a club high. South crosses in trumps and ruffs another club high. South draws the last trump ending in dummy and has a good club set up for a heart loser.
